title: Benoni Defense: the ideas
line: An unbalanced game: Black has more pawns on the queen's side, White more in the center.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Bring the knight out. For now it stops White's other center pawn from coming to e4.
Push the pawn on c7 two squares. It attacks White's pawn on d4 from the side.

also.e7e6: That leads to the Nimzo-Indian or the Queen's Indian, also sound. This lesson goes on with the side pawn.

steps.after: White pushes past. This is the Benoni Defense.

steps.text: Attack the pawn on d5 with the pawn in front of your king.

also.b7b5: That is the Benko Gambit, a pawn for open files. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.

steps.after: Now Black has more pawns on the queen's side, and White more in the center.

steps.text: Move the pawn in front of your queen one square. It holds back White's center pawns.
steps.after: Black takes on risk for an unbalanced game: White's extra center pawns can come forward fast.

steps.text: Push the pawn on g7 one square, to make room for your bishop.
steps.after: White pushes another pawn forward. This is the sharpest line.

steps.text: Put the bishop on the long diagonal. Once your knight moves, it aims at White's queen's side.
Block the check with the knight from f6, not the one from b8. Then a pawn push to e5 hits no knight.

wrong.b8d7: Then White's pawn pushes to e5 and hits your other knight, and Black is in trouble.
wrong.c8d7: That blocks too, but the engine rates it clearly weaker: White trades bishops and keeps its big center.

steps.after: Your pawn and bishop guard e5, and Black can castle next.

summary: Black trades a center pawn to get more pawns on the queen's side. Against the sharpest line, block the check with care.
